thoughts.content: I'll start with history to see if this matches a known pattern, then verify with fresh evidence from the live cluster.

Found one open incident matching this exact alert (likely this one). Prior frontend history is about a different alert type (KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck from image tag typo) — not CrashLooping. That's a different mechanism; I will not assume it applies here. Let's get fresh evidence from the live cluster.

Hypothesis: pod crash looping could be OOM (like worker's past issue), bad config/env change, or probe failure. Testing by checking current pod status first.

New ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589 has one pod crash looping (3 restarts in 71s) while old ReplicaSet pods run fine. This is an active rollout due to a config change. Let's inspect the crashing pod's logs, events, and the new ReplicaSet's config to find what changed.

Confirmed: nginx fails to start with nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9 — a config syntax error (typo: missing "n" in "connect"). This is the root cause: a ConfigMap-sourced nginx config change introduced a syntax error. The old ReplicaSet's pods are untouched/already-running so they don't re-parse the config, but any new pod reading the current ConfigMap fails immediately. Let's confirm the ConfigMap content and check deployment history/events to establish exactly what changed and when.

The ConfigMap frontend-nginx currently contains the typo proxy_conect_timeout (should be proxy_connect_timeout), matching the last-applied-configuration annotation — meaning it was applied via kubectl apply, not a live edit, and is baked into the ConfigMap's desired state. rollout history is blocked by policy (mutating-kubectl denylist). Let me verify whether the old (healthy) ReplicaSet's pods also hit this nginx config error at their own startup — this will tell us whether the ConfigMap already had the typo when they started.

Strong finding: the Deployment's live spec confirms revision 2 was triggered by a kubectl rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00 = 15:00:12 UTC) — only 9 seconds after the namespace was created (15:00:03Z). The old pod (revision 1, ReplicaSet frontend-76d98597b9) is still logging healthy 200 OK responses as of 15:02:34 — it started before/at the point the ConfigMap had bad content and its already-running nginx master process never reparsed the file. The new pod (revision 2, ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589) started fresh after the restart, read the current (broken) ConfigMap, and nginx failed its startup config validation. This explains both the crash loop AND why 2/2 old pods are still serving traffic fine — it's a stuck rolling update, not a full outage.

Let me check incident/blast-radius context to complete the picture.

Root Cause: CONFIRMED

Symptom actively occurring: kubectl get pods -n shop shows frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr in CrashLoopBackOff, Restart Count 3, Last State Terminated/Error/Exit Code 1 (as of investigation time).

Mechanism (direct evidence):
``
kubectl logs frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr -n shop --previous
2026/10/02 15:01:36 [emerg] 1#1: unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
`
The ConfigMap frontend-nginx (mounted at /etc/nginx/conf.d) contains a typo: proxy_conect_timeout instead of proxy_connect_timeout. This is baked into the ConfigMap's last-applied-configuration annotation, i.e., it was applied deliberately via kubectl apply, not a stray live edit. nginx validates its entire config at every container start and refuses to boot on an unknown directive — exit 1, repeat → CrashLoopBackOff.

Why only the new pod crashes, not all of them: The Deployment's live spec shows kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00 (15:00:12 UTC) on the pod template — a kubectl rollout restart was issued just 9 seconds after the ConfigMap/Deployment were created (15:00:03Z), spawning new ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589.
